note: Twenty-one measured regions over nineteen of twenty-nine pages, resolving into 16 figure rows, 3 printed tables and 2 exclusions (the p1 summary-sheet form and the p21 tail of Table 2), with nothing unresolved and no declared gaps. Families: 11 `line`, 3 `scatter`, 3 `table-grid`, 1 `heatmap-or-contour` and 1 `flowchart-or-schematic`. Nineteen printed figure numbers resolve into fifteen numbered rows and one uncaptioned flowchart, because five raster regions carry two numbered exhibits each and Figures 2 to 7 carry three sub-panels apiece in a 2x2 plate with one cell empty. The numbering is the colon form 'Figure 1:' to 'Figure 19:' against a bare 'Table 1' to 'Table 3'; every caption is in the text layer and every caption prints below its art; and no exhibit is cited by number anywhere - all seventeen pointers are deictic, three of them running backwards onto the page before their plate. Faults worth carrying downstream: Figures 5 and 6 switch the same x variable between a 0 to 1 and a 0 to 100 scale, Figure 5's axis is titled 'bic car fraction', Figure 7's typeset sub-captions are swapped against its in-image titles, Figure 13's caption misspells 'Factor score' as 'Factor sore', the p27 plate reuses 'Figure 12' as the number and title of a different chart, and Figure 1 is a printed-digit state lattice rather than a plot.
rules: The numbering is the colon form throughout - 'Figure 1:' to 'Figure 19:' - except for the three tables, which print a bare 'Table 1', 'Table 2' and 'Table 3' with no title and no stop, so `caption.numbering` is 'Figure N:' for the figures and 'Table N' for the tables [caption.numbering].

Five measured regions each carry two separately numbered exhibits, and the layout pass cannot split them: the p17 plate holds Figures 8 and 9, p18 holds 10 and 11, p23 holds 13 and 14, and p26 holds 17 and 18, all as one raster each. One row per region is mandatory (`record.py` refuses a region counted twice), so each of those rows quotes both printed captions in print order and carries `panel_count` for the plot panels it holds [geometry.panel_count].

Figures 2 to 7 are three-quarters of a 2x2 plate each, with panel a top left, b top right, c bottom left and the bottom-right cell empty; the typeset sub-captions print below the panels and the text layer reads them in a different order from the letters ('b', then 'a', then 'c'), so the quoted caption keeps the printed order rather than the reading order [caption.verbatim].

No exhibit in this paper is cited by number in prose. Every pointer is deictic - 'the flowchart below', 'the figures show that', 'compare this two figures', 'get following curves', 'the following are figures of flow, lane change frequency and average speed' - so all sixteen figure rows and all three tables record an empty style list and `count` 0, with the pointer sentence quoted from the page it prints on [mention.lead_pattern].

Three of those deictic pointers run backwards: the p25 sentence 'The following are figures of flow, lane change frequency and average speed' introduces the p26 and p27 plates, and the p22 sentence that introduces the factor-score curves is reused for the p23 plate, so those rows carry a negative `lead_pages` [mention.lead_pages].

Table 2 breaks over the page boundary: five of its eight rows print on page 20 and the x6 to x8 rows on page 21 with the merged title and header repeated. It is counted once on the p20 band with `continued` true, and the p21 band is excluded `split-across-pages` [table.continued].

All three tables are one construction - a merged title cell, an empty spacer row, a header row of four factor columns over a blank stub, rules under the title and the header and between every body row, full-height vertical rules and a complete outer frame, with no zebra anywhere - so all three are `vertical-rules` with `merged_cells` true and decimal-aligned statistics [table.rule_style].

Every caption in this paper is in the text layer, tables included, and every caption prints below its grid or chart, so no caption is typed from the crop and no table is captioned above [caption.position].

The one uncaptioned exhibit is the p5 flowchart, which the prose introduces with 'The analyzing procedure can be illustrated by the flowchart below:' and never numbers. It is recorded with an empty caption, `caption_source` none and numbering none [caption.numbering].

Figure 1 is a state lattice, not a plot: each cell of a two-block space-time grid prints the number of vehicles in that section, with only bare 'Space' and 'Time' arrow axes, so it is recorded `heatmap-or-contour` rather than `line` [geometry.family].

Families follow what is drawn, not what a caption promises: Figures 2, 3 and 4 are connected line charts with square markers and Figures 5, 6 and 7 are unconnected point clouds, so the first three are `line` and the last three `scatter`, although all six are captioned the same way [geometry.family].

The factor-score plates key six series each and put the key outside, below the plot, in two blocks - solid for traffic flow, dashed for safety - with the x-variable name used as the legend header instead of an axis title, so `legend` is 'below' on Figures 12 to 16 and 'inside' on the p17, p18, p26 and p27 plates [geometry.legend].

mention.lead_sentence: We use principal component method to estimate the factor loading matrix, and get the eigenvalues of the correlation matrix

tables.note: The eigenvalue table, a boxed SPSS-style grid: a merged title cell reading 'Eigenvalues of the Correlation Matrix: Total = 8 Average = 1' across all five columns, a header row of Eigenvalue, Difference, Proportion, Cumulative over a blank stub, then eight numbered rows. Full-height vertical rules between every column, an outer frame on all four sides, a rule under the header and a rule between every body row, decimal-aligned statistics and no zebra. Row 8 prints an empty Difference cell, which is blank rather than merged. The caption is the bare word 'Table 1' below the grid, with no title [table.merged_cells].

mention.lead_sentence: Then we apply the orthogonal rotation that has the biggest variance to the factor loading matrix, and get the rotated factor pattern:

tables.note: The rotated factor pattern, split over the page break: a merged title cell 'Rotated Factor Pattern' with an empty spacer row beneath it, a header row of Factor1 to Factor4 over a blank stub, then eight rows x1 to x8 loaded -0.89 to 0.90. Five rows print on page 20 and the last three on page 21 with the title and header repeated, so the row carries `continued` true and the p21 band is excluded `split-across-pages`. The caption 'Table 2' prints on page 21 under the tail, not under the p20 band [table.continued].

mention.lead_sentence: After that, we use Thompson factor to calculate the scores of F1, F2, F3 and F4, and get the following form of standardized scoring coefficients:

tables.note: The standardized scoring coefficients in the same boxed construction: merged title cell 'Standardized Scoring Coefficients', a header row of Factor1 to Factor4 over a blank stub, eight rows x1 to x8, vertical rules full height, outer frame, no zebra. The coefficients here are the ones the p22 equations print, so the table and the three factor-score formulas can be cross-checked digit by digit; the caption is the bare 'Table 3' below the grid [table.rule_style].
